# E.18 setup

## Contract

The Product Owner explicitly authorizes activation, YOLO execution, companion repositories and final origin push. Only E.18 and necessary shared documents change. SQLcl PROJECT and Actions retain native responsibilities. No credentials are stored in scratch. No prior completion assertion counts as fresh evidence. Token accounting is unavailable.

## Analysis

[PBI-086](../../BACKLOG.md#pbi-086-measure-complete-pipeline-feedback-and-runner-capacity) and [PLAN](../../PLAN.md#sprint-e18---measure-complete-pipeline-feedback-and-runner-capacity) require complete workload timing on the E.17 baseline. E.17 source has JDK, pinned SQLcl, Oracle, APEX, ORDS and native release checks; utPLSQL must be added to the measured workload. Fresh hosted jobs preserve candidate isolation. The primary actor is SRS A-03 Delivery operator, supported by A-05 Git hosting service; browser validation exercises A-04 application-user behavior. Actions, Oracle and the project-owned pipeline remain internal components under the [SRS actor model](../../docs/srs.md#actors). The operator dispatches a declared experiment, inspects phase/resource/queue receipts, compares distributions and chooses capacity without dropping validation.

## Decisions

Use an Elaboration executable measurement prototype, retaining all E.17 native checks. Use two replicas per serial/concurrent trial and explicitly describe small-sample percentile limits. Cold means a unique empty per-run dependency-cache key; warm means a verified cache hit, not a reused database. Database state remains job-private. No ten-minute process cutoff supersedes the user instruction to persist.
# E.18 implementation record

## Current verified state

Measured source capacity-v1 at aea3a77 passes all four two-replica cells. [Report](capacity_report.md) derives timings/resources/recommendations from actual receipts; [checklist](sprint_E.18_checklist.md) owns acceptance coverage. Separate live revision 920b1c4 passes both complete replicas and preserves blank-login/final-result captures. All six new/full gates pass, including unfiltered 27/27 integration with stable executable-source snapshots and scoped cleanup. Presentation/handover technical review passes; the final audit and lifecycle transaction are recorded in the handover and closure records. The historical trial sections below are retained observations, not the current status.

## Initial exploratory execution — historical

Dedicated repository: https://github.com/rstyczynski/APEX_CICD_E.18 at f2be037f2bbd6a3f8757954077e6c9c811f5d041. Maintained source is mirrored in [sprint-work/E.18](../../sprint-work/E.18/). [Design](sprint_E.18_design.md) owns measurement definitions and [checklist](sprint_E.18_checklist.md) tracks acceptance.

Cold serial run 45844508366, cold concurrent run 45844673934 and warm-cache population run 45844682312 are dispatched. All are pending. Population runs are excluded from warm measurements. Jobs run on independent hosted machines; concurrency here measures runner slots and batch completion, not competing databases on one host. Aggregate host counters include the runner and background services. Five-second sampling can miss short peaks. GitHub job start minus workflow creation combines scheduling, capacity queueing and deliberate serial admission; it does not isolate GitHub infrastructure queueing.

The observer records CPU counters, available memory and root-disk free space without collecting process command lines or credentials. Actions API step timestamps provide phase durations; native result files validate successful work. Download caches are verified by the original archive checksums on every use. Database images and utPLSQL source remain pinned. JDK retains E.17's major-version setup policy; exact installed build is a reported measurement input, not an invented immutable pin.

## Initial source checks

A1 source smoke and A2 arithmetic contracts pass 1/1 each. They establish syntax, named E.17 step retention and report arithmetic only. Native execution and cache-hit qualification remain pending. No production performance conclusion follows from these checks.

## UI capture recovery

The browser connector returned “The browser access host is unavailable”. Native Chrome control was available and used to inspect the real first trial. [Gallery](screenshots/index.html) preserves the starting window and framed copy. The failed connector did not block UI inspection.

## Corrected trials

After preserving the initial installer failure, source d878df0 dispatches corrected cold serial 45845297753, cold concurrent 45845306173 and cache population 45845314659. Initial exploratory trials preceded the persisted design specification and are not acceptance samples. The corrected trials follow that specification. The native installer log redacts its vendor-default schema password; job-generated private passwords remain masked.

Source 1470fb3 replaces the exploratory arithmetic-only test with the existing five-case backend/API fixtures, unchanged from tests/sql/backend and examples/testable-backend. Source aea3a77 executes the suite as E5_TEST, avoiding SYS invoker inheritance. Current cold serial 45846143379, cold concurrent 45846150456 and cache population 45846157988 follow the persisted design; each starts independent databases and retains the full E.17 lifecycle. Earlier trial IDs are diagnostic only.

## Measured-source freeze and live capture revision

Both cache population replicas in 45846157988 pass. The measured source is frozen as tag capacity-v1 at aea3a771cac687fa32ac09d24faf6d2d55bd2342. Warm serial 45848134832 and warm concurrent 45848140354 dispatch that exact tag, matching cold trials 45846143379/45846150456. Warm population is excluded. Live demonstration 45848145737 dispatches separate main source 920b1c4, which adds a blank-login screenshot before entering private inputs. Its timings are excluded from the comparison. This preserves source equivalence for all eight measured samples while recording the complete application UI transition in the demonstration.

## P2. Project lifecycle phases set emphasis; they do not prohibit refinement

The project lifecycle remains Inception, Elaboration, Construction, and Transition. These phases establish the dominant emphasis of the work:

- Inception emphasizes business context, vision, requirements, scope, and major risks.
- Elaboration emphasizes architecture, risk retirement, design, and validation.
- Construction emphasizes implementation and testing.
- Transition emphasizes deployment, stabilization, and user feedback.

All disciplines remain open to refinement in later iterations. In particular, business modeling and requirements are mostly established early, but evidence from design, implementation, testing, or use may require them to be revisited.

## P3. Sprint wrap-up is not necessarily project Transition

The RUP Strikes Back wrap-up phase completes and documents a sprint. It does not by itself mean that the product has entered the project-level Transition phase or is ready for release. Project-level Transition occurs when the project plan declares release, deployment, and adoption activities to be the dominant focus.

## P4. A sprint may deliver multiple coherent outcomes

A sprint may contain multiple independently coherent backlog items when they share a common iteration objective, have manageable dependencies, and can be reviewed together. This is particularly appropriate for Inception and Elaboration, where one iteration can establish several connected artifacts such as requirements, risks, scope, and an architecture baseline.

Each backlog item must retain its own value statement and acceptance signal. The sprint design and wrap-up must identify the evidence for each item, so grouping does not hide incomplete work or weaken traceability. Split items into separate sprints when their dependencies, risk, approval needs, or validation methods would make a single review unclear.

## P5. Process entry point and local method adoption

The project root `BACKLOG.md` is the source of Product Owner priorities. The project root `PLAN.md` is the source of sprint selection and status. When installed, the root `RUP_patch.md` points to `RUPStrikesBack.patch/RUP_patch.md`, which defines local policy that supplements or overrides the generic method in the `RUPStrikesBack` submodule.

Sprint 0 is marked `Progress` by the bootstrap plan. To execute it, the Product Owner explicitly invokes the Codex `rup-strikes-back` skill in the declared mode. For a later planned sprint, the Product Owner first changes that sprint’s status in the root `PLAN.md` from `Planned` to `Progress`, then explicitly invokes the skill. The agent reads its manager and selected phase procedures from `.agents/skills/rup-strikes-back/references/`, then applies this local patch before executing the sprint.

`rup-strikes-back` is the Codex method entry point. The submodule's `/rup-manager` is a Claude compatibility command, not a native Codex command. Managed mode remains the default: the agent pauses for Product Owner approval at the defined decision points.

## P6. Refine prototype work into hierarchical sub-PBIs

When an accepted Inception architecture identifies a prototype PBI that spans
several independently reviewable pieces of work, the following Elaboration
iteration must refine that parent PBI before prototype construction. This is a
required planning checkpoint, not permission to invent the work during
Inception.

Use hierarchical identifiers in the form `PBI-XX.YY`, where `PBI-XX` is the
accepted parent PBI and `YY` is a sequential child number. For example,
`PBI-011.1`, `PBI-011.2`, and `PBI-011.3` are child work items of `PBI-011`.

Create the child items during the Elaboration sprint's setup/design phase, in
the active sprint's design record. Each child item must state its parent, its
bounded outcome, its acceptance evidence, and its dependency on other child
items. Record the same identifiers on the progress board for status tracking.

Child sub-PBIs are sprint-scoped refinements of their parent, not new
Product-Owner backlog items. Keep the parent PBI in the root `BACKLOG.md` and
`PLAN.md`; promote a child to a new root backlog item only when it gains
independent product value, priority, or deferral authority. In managed mode,
the Product Owner approves the proposed decomposition before prototype
construction starts.

          printf 'altered' >> "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/result/substituted.zip"
          if python3 "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/provenance.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/result/substituted.zip" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/result/receipt-1.1.0.json" "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" '25.4.1.022.0618' > "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/result/reject-substituted-bytes.txt" 2>&1; then exit 1; fi
          grep -qx 'artifact mismatch' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/result/reject-substituted-bytes.txt"
      - name: Assert refusal cases preserved target
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/native
        run: |
          bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/sql.sh" native-target negative-after <<'SQL'
          select id,message,extra from preserved;
          SQL
          cmp "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/result/negative-before.log" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/result/negative-after.log"
          git bundle create "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/result/native-history.bundle" --all
          jq -n --arg source "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" '{native_install:true,native_upgrade:true,native_repeat:true,preserved:true,negatives:["artifact","source","tool","substituted-bytes"],source:$source}' > "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/result/success.json"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - name: Install declared browser test dependencies
        run: |
          npm install --no-save playwright@1.56.1
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Verify application after native delivery
        run: |
          python3 provision_host.py verify
          node browser.mjs
      - name: Clean job-private connection material
        if: always()
        run: |
          rm -rf "$RUNNER_TEMP/private-sqlcl" "$RUNNER_TEMP/e17-private"
          docker rm -f e17-ords e17-author e17-target || true
          test ! -e "$RUNNER_TEMP/private-sqlcl"
          test ! -e "$RUNNER_TEMP/e17-private"
          echo 'PASS private inputs removed' > result/cleanup.txt
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/wrong-receipt.json"
      - name: Finish resource observations
        if: always()
        env:
          CACHE_HIT: ${{ steps.dependencies.outputs.cache-hit }}
          CACHE_MODE: ${{ inputs.cache }}
          PARALLEL: ${{ inputs.parallel }}
          REPLICA: ${{ matrix.replica }}
        run: |
          kill "$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/sampler.pid")" || true
          free -b > result/memory-end.txt
          df -B1 > result/disk-end.txt
          python3 - <<'PYCODE'
          import json,os
          from pathlib import Path
          Path('result/measurement.json').write_text(json.dumps({k:os.environ[k] for k in ['CACHE_HIT','CACHE_MODE','PARALLEL','REPLICA','GITHUB_RUN_ID','GITHUB_SHA']}))
          PYCODE

        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: native-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ matrix.replica }}
          path: result/
name: Trusted Oracle validation
run-name: Oracle ${{ inputs.correlation || github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      correlation:
        type: string
        required: true
      candidate_pr:
        type: string
        required: false
      inspection_pause:
        type: boolean
        default: false
        required: false
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: oracle-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  oracle:
    name: Oracle candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    services:
      oracle:
        image: gvenzl/oracle-free@sha256:cebd977833411a42170777d8e9ccf616a028a2bb137ae96498354ab6c7510268
        env:
          ORACLE_RANDOM_PASSWORD: 'yes'
          APP_USER: candidate
          APP_USER_PASSWORD: Disposable_Candidate_15
        ports:
          - 127.0.0.1:1521:1521
        options: >-
          --health-cmd healthcheck.sh --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 40
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Initialize private sentinel
        env:
          ORACLE_CONTAINER: ${{ job.services.oracle.id }}
        run: |
          docker exec -i "$ORACLE_CONTAINER" sqlplus -s / as sysdba <<'SQL'
          whenever sqlerror exit failure
          alter session set container=FREEPDB1;
          create table system.e15_private (value varchar2(80));
          insert into system.e15_private values ('private sentinel');
          commit;
          SQL
      - name: Challenge publication authority
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh api --method POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/statuses/$GITHUB_SHA" -f state=success -f context=Unauthorized > publication.log 2>&1; then
            echo 'Unexpected publication authority'; exit 1
          fi
          cat publication.log
          grep -q 'HTTP 403' publication.log
      - name: Bind companion candidate as data
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.candidate_pr != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ inputs.candidate_pr }}
        run: |
          case "$PR" in *[!0-9]*|'') echo 'Invalid PR number'; exit 1;; esac
          gh api "repos/rstyczynski/APEX_CICD_E.18-candidates/pulls/$PR" > candidate-event.json
          python3 - <<'PYCODE'
          import json, os, re
          from pathlib import Path
          event = json.loads(Path('candidate-event.json').read_text())
          assert event['state'] == 'open' and event['base']['ref'] == 'main'
          head, base = event['head']['sha'], event['base']['sha']
          assert re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{40}', head) and re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{40}', base)
          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_ENV'], 'a') as f:
              f.write('E15_SOURCE_HEAD=' + head + '\nE15_SOURCE_BASE=' + base + '\n')
          print('COMPANION SOURCE', head, 'BASE', base)
          PYCODE
          SOURCE_HEAD=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('candidate-event.json'))['head']['sha'])")
          gh api "repos/rstyczynski/APEX_CICD_E.18-candidates/contents/candidate.sql?ref=$SOURCE_HEAD" -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json' > candidate.sql
      - name: Obtain candidate SQL as data
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CANDIDATE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/contents/candidate.sql?ref=$CANDIDATE" -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json' > candidate.sql
      - name: Verify trusted Review matches candidate bytes
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' || inputs.candidate_pr != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          SOURCE_REPO: ${{ inputs.candidate_pr != '' && 'rstyczynski/APEX_CICD_E.18-candidates' || github.repository }}
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || env.E15_SOURCE_BASE }}
          HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || env.E15_SOURCE_HEAD }}
        run: |
          gh api "repos/$SOURCE_REPO/compare/$BASE...$HEAD" --jq '[.files[].filename]' > changed.json
          python3 - <<'PYCODE'
          import hashlib, json
          from pathlib import Path
          assert json.loads(Path('changed.json').read_text()) == ['candidate.sql'], 'unreviewed files'
          report = json.loads(Path('review.json').read_text())
          assert report['decision'] == 'accept'
          assert hashlib.sha256(Path('candidate.sql').read_bytes()).hexdigest() == report['sql_sha256'], 'stale Review'
          print('PASS trusted Review matches candidate bytes; candidate report cannot replace base report')
          PYCODE
      - name: Install Oracle driver
        run: python3 -m pip install oracledb==3.4.1
      - name: Execute bounded application-user SQL
        env:
          CANDIDATE_PASSWORD: Disposable_Candidate_15
        run: python3 validate.py

      - name: Inspection interval
        if: inputs.inspection_pause
        run: sleep 60

  publish:
    name: Trusted publisher
    needs: oracle
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      checks: write
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Publish only current candidate outcome
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || env.E15_SOURCE_HEAD }}
          BASE: ${{ github.sha }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ needs.oracle.result }}
        run: |
          test "$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/pulls/$NUMBER" --jq .head.sha)" = "$HEAD"
          test "$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/main" --jq .sha)" = "$BASE"
          result=failure
          if test "$OUTCOME" = success; then result=success; fi
          gh api --method POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/check-runs" -f name=Integrated -f head_sha="$HEAD" -f status=completed -f conclusion="$result"
"}

"""Snapshot accessible native session records; never reconstruct unavailable turns."""
import datetime,json,os,re
from pathlib import Path
thread=os.environ['CODEX_THREAD_ID']
files=list((Path.home()/'.codex/sessions').rglob('*'+thread+'*.jsonl'))
root=Path(__file__).parent/'chat';root.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
ts=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ')
base=f'{ts}_{thread}'
records=[]
for f in files:
 for line in f.read_text().splitlines():
  try: records.append(json.loads(line))
  except json.JSONDecodeError: pass
# Redact credential-shaped values without reading unrelated authentication stores.
raw='\n'.join(json.dumps(r,ensure_ascii=False) for r in records)+'\n'
raw=re.sub(r'(?i)(gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}|[REDACTED credential]\\\n]*)','[REDACTED credential]',raw)
(root/(base+'.jsonl')).write_text(raw)
parsed=[json.loads(l) for l in raw.splitlines() if l]
md=['# Accessible native session snapshot','',f'Thread: {thread}. Export: {ts}. Initial execution; no --continue observed.','', 'Coverage: all complete JSONL records accessible at snapshot time. Native writer may lag; records after export are absent. No completeness claim. Credential-shaped values explicitly redacted where matched.','']
for i,r in enumerate(parsed,1):
 md.extend([f'## Record {i}: {r.get("type","unknown")}','', '```json',json.dumps(r,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2),'```',''])
(root/(base+'.md')).write_text('\n'.join(md))
index=root/'index.md'
if not index.exists():index.write_text('# E.19 chat snapshots\n\nNative local session JSONL read interface. ## Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need to download Node.js and create a public {% data variables.product.prodname_dotcom %} repository.

  1. Download and install Node.js 24.x, which includes npm.

  2. Create a new public repository on {% data variables.product.github %} and call it "hello-world-javascript-action". For more information, see AUTOTITLE.

  3. Clone your repository to your computer. For more information, see AUTOTITLE.

  4. From your terminal, change directories into your new repository.
    
    cd hello-world-javascript-action

  5. From your terminal, initialize the directory with npm to generate a `package.json` file.
    
    npm init -y

## Creating an action metadata file

Create a new file named `action.yml` in the `hello-world-javascript-action` directory with the following example code. For more information, see AUTOTITLE.
    
    name: Hello World
    description: Greet someone and record the time
    
    inputs:
      who-to-greet: # id of input
        description: Who to greet
        required: true
        default: World
    
    outputs:
      time: # id of output
        description: The time we greeted you
    
    runs:
      using: node24
      main: dist/index.js

This file defines the `who-to-greet` input and `time` output. It also tells the action runner how to start running this JavaScript action.

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > sprint-work/E.19/CATALOGUE.md <<'EOF' # JavaScript support action catalogue — initial slice These actions use the GitHub runner's Node 24 action runtime. They need no npm dependencies, setup-node, Python installation or Python execution. A runner supporting node24 is required. The metadata runtime is documented by [GitHub](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/metadata-syntax#runs-for-javascript-actions). ## Tool compatibility `actions/tool` requires `log` (SQLcl version output) and `config` (native `.dbtools/project.config.json`). It validates release 25.4.1.0, qualified build 25.4.1.022.0618 and matching native metadata. Missing metadata is rejected, deliberately tightening the old helper's optional-file behavior to enforce AGENTS.md/NFR-5. It does not launch SQLcl or establish that the supplied log came from the current executable; the workflow must capture it immediately before native processing. ## Native output `actions/output` requires `log`, the actual native tool output. It rejects empty output, common native error signatures and nonzero Errors counts after stripping ANSI color sequences. This complements the native process exit status; a clean text file alone does not prove command execution or semantic correctness. ## Provenance `actions/provenance` requires `archive`, `receipt` (JSON containing source, build, sha256), `source` (expected 40-character lowercase Git SHA) and `build` (actual qualified build). It binds exact archive bytes to independently supplied source/build expectations. Every mismatch throws an explicit error; runtime optimization cannot disable it. Receipt authenticity and expected-source authority are workflow responsibilities. ## Shared behavior and usage All three emit `validated=true` only after success and return nonzero on a missing file, final-component symlink, malformed input or failed check. They never mutate a target. Use ordinary GitHub Actions success dependencies to prevent deployment after rejection. Do not set continue-on-error on a production guard. The qualification workflow deliberately uses it to inspect an expected rejection. Check out this repository at a reviewed immutable commit and invoke a local action: ```yaml - uses: ./actions/tool with: log: result/tool.txt config: .dbtools/project.config.json - uses: ./actions/output with: log: result/native-command.log - uses: ./actions/provenance with: archive: result/release.zip receipt: result/receipt.json source: ${{ steps.reviewed-source.outputs.sha }} build: ${{ steps.actual-tool.outputs.build }} ``` This is a wiring example requiring real producer steps and reviewed files, not a runnable native delivery demonstration. Full qualification and inventory remain pending; see the progress repository's E.19 checklist. EOF cat > progress/E.19/sprint_E.19_inventory.md <<'EOF' # E.19 initial inventory ## Examined sources The tracked `sprint-work/` Python inventory contains E.15 controller/validator, E.16 three checks, E.17 their copies plus provisioner/validator, and E.18 those five plus resource sampling. Current latest native workflow was read from the retained E.18 checkout `.github/workflows/native.yml`; hosted candidate workflow `.github/workflows/oracle.yml` was also inspected. Repository-wide and remote-source completeness remain to be verified. ## Initial migration scope E.16/E.17/E.18 `check_tool.py`, `check_output.py`, `provenance.py` are repeated pure support checks. The E.19 shared implementation replaces their current logic without editing historical files. The provenance asserts are replaced by explicit exceptions. Tool metadata becomes mandatory, consistent with NFR-5. Original copies remain historical acceptance/benchmark inputs. E.18 `provision_host.py` provides disposable host setup and application provisioning. E.18 `sample_resources.py` measures resources. E.15 `controller.py` owns the historical custom controller. These are initially classified outside pure supporting-check migration, with historical use preserved. This disposition does not authorize adding a new lifecycle controller or claiming a Python-free complete native workflow. The embedded supporting checks and current-use status still require complete review before accepting the inventory. E.15/E.17/E.18 `validate.py` executes actual Oracle application checks; it must be examined separately from pure file checks. Inline Python in oracle.yml verifies candidate metadata, exact trusted Review bytes and freshness. Those inline supporting checks require migration or a justified disposition; they are not silently excluded. No OCI interaction has been found in the initial three checks. Full source inventory remains open. EOF cat > progress/E.19/sprint_E.19_checklist.md <<'EOF' # E.19 requirement-to-evidence checklist ## Mandatory acceptance — BACKLOG PBI-087 Inventory every workflow Python support check and document dispositions: partial, [initial inventory](sprint_E.19_inventory.md); completeness pending. Provide discoverable reusable action catalogue, purpose/inputs/outputs/failures/usage: initial three actions implemented in [catalogue](../../sprint-work/E.19/CATALOGUE.md), broader inventory pending. Remove migrated checks' Python dependency and optimization-sensitive provenance assertions: implemented in initial three-action slice, explicit JavaScript exceptions; [local tests](tests/initial-unit.log) pass 3 test groups. Hosted source 6b6a412 uses Node action runtime and no Python command. Demonstrate every in-scope check through catalogued actions in real GitHub workflows with valid, malformed/missing inputs and source/artifact/tool mismatches before mutation: partial. [Run 45873741697](https://github.com/rstyczynski/APEX_CICD_E.19/actions/runs/45873741697) executes all three valid actions and malformed provenance rejection with skipped filesystem mutation sentinel. Other negative contracts run as unit functions, not yet every catalogued-action case. Synthetic file fixtures do not establish real SQLcl/Oracle target behavior. Preserve native technology responsibilities and historical evidence: initial implementation performs checks only; old evidence retained. Native workflow migration pending. Acceptance and full smoke/unit/integration regression: pending. Initial Node unit tests do not satisfy all six RUP gates. ## Mandatory plan additions — PLAN E.19 Equivalent Python/JavaScript workloads and runner conditions; versions, counts, cold/warm setup/check/overall timings; installation/dependency/maintenance assessment: pending. Preinstalled Python must not be reported as installation cost. No performance benefit claimed. Official OCI JavaScript SDK for any needed OCI interactions: none selected so far; full inventory pending. ## Mandatory execution instructions and method Screenshots: two real Chrome application-window captures retained; [gallery](screenshots/index.html) pending rendering/navigation verification. Opening workflow summary and job detail captured after actions occurred; no earlier dispatch capture exists. Chat archive: [index](chat/index.md) records native JSONL snapshots and readable companions with writer-lag limits. Snapshot refresh required before handover/final response. Demonstration, PPTX walkthrough pair, manual, rendered-slide review, documentation audit, completed-increment commits and closure: pending. No Product Owner reaction or acceptance invented. ## Implementation choices Three native node24 actions sharing dependency-free CommonJS logic; regular-file validation; explicit throws; synthetic fixture sentinel. These are design choices, not extra acceptance requirements. ## Blocker audit No external blocker is established. Remaining items are implementation and verification work, not grounds for closure or a blocker claim. Browser connector is unavailable, but native Chrome control succeeded. No authorization clarification is needed. EOF cat > progress/E.19/screenshots/index.html <<'EOF' E.19 screenshot evidence

E.19 hosted contract execution

Real Chrome application-window captures, execution order. Synthetic check fixtures; no Oracle target claim. Requirement checklist · Run record

1. Open completed hosted run

Opened job details. Valid tool/output/provenance steps succeeded. Expected provenance failure was tolerated for test inspection; downstream mutation sentinel was skipped and assertion passed. Detailed expected-error text is in the execution log, not expanded in this capture.

# E.18 test execution results

## Verified result

All six required gates pass without waived failures. New A1 smoke, A2 unit and A3 integration pass one manifest entry each. Full B1 smoke passes 17/17, B2 unit passes 19/19 and B3 integration passes 27/27; the wrapper exits zero after source-stability and scoped-cleanup checks. These are manifest/function counts, not counts of unique native scenarios. [Checklist](sprint_E.18_checklist.md) maps acceptance, [report](capacity_report.md) owns measured results, and [handover](sprint_E.18_handover.md) records demonstration and artifact review.

## What the checks establish

A1 checks workflow/Bash/Python syntax, retention of every named E.17 native stage and byte equality with the existing backend SQL fixtures. A2 uses explicitly synthetic inputs to check statistic arithmetic, missing/failed records and warm-cache-miss refusal; it makes no performance claim. A3 reads actual successful workflow metadata/artifacts for four two-replica cells, binds source/run identity, requires complete native/backend/browser/cleanup success, verifies cold/warm admission, confirms actual serial/concurrent overlap and derives phase/resource statistics. All eight samples use aea3a771cac687fa32ac09d24faf6d2d55bd2342. Forty backend case executions represent five distinct behaviors repeated across eight samples.

The [cohort audit](tests/cohort-isolation.log) additionally checks eight distinct runner execution identities and sixteen author/target namespaces with bound source/run and private cleanup. A repeated hostname in two nonoverlapping jobs is recorded as a physical-identity/warmth limit. [Live verification](tests/live-demo-verification.log) independently checks both complete replicas at 920b1c4a15eaafb000ce73c432322efa20e247f1, including blank-login capture and actual authenticated retained-row rendering. Its timings and population run 45846157988 are excluded from the comparison.

B1/B2 re-run every existing source/platform/unit entry. B3 replays the existing complete historical integration manifest against the owned isolated local fixture and the new acceptance reader. It also dispatches a fresh real Oracle GitHub workflow in the E.18 repository: run 45855180342 at 920b1c4 passes the real greeting, private-table denial and unauthorized-publication HTTP 403 checks. The native E.16 and clean-host E.17 readers revalidate immutable qualified receipts/runs 45810907563 and 45828709006, plus their linked review controls; new downloads are not new native delivery executions. Local review/capability tests retain their documented local/synthetic boundaries.

The historical fixture deliberately uses its qualified SQLcl 25.3.0.274.1210 state; the measured native E.18 projects use qualified 25.4.1.022.0618 and metadata 25.4.1.0. No project version was edited to bypass a native check. Prepared-host regression remains separate from fresh hosted workload qualification. [Test profile](../../docs/test-profile.md#e18-pipeline-capacity-experiment) owns invocation and scope.

## Full-regression evidence preservation

The [replay index](tests/regression-replay/index.json) maps exact generated outputs to their original execution paths and hashes. Sixty-two tracked historical test outputs were restored byte for byte, and 162 new generated files were moved into E.18 after hash checks. [Restoration receipt](tests/regression-replay/restoration-receipt.txt) confirms no historical source/user changes were reverted. Raw paths/timestamps remain as recorded, including host-local timestamps in some historical filenames. These are current regression observations, not rewritten historical acceptance.

[Before-source snapshot](tests/regression-replay/progress/E.12/tests/legacy-regression/run-20261126T164709-4128/source-snapshot-before.json) and [after-source snapshot](tests/regression-replay/progress/E.12/tests/legacy-regression/run-20261126T164709-4128/source-snapshot-after.json) are equal. The full wrapper's successful exit includes that check and private fixture cleanup.

## Failure history and limits

[BUG-18.1/18.2](sprint_E.18_bugs.md) preserve real exploratory installer/privilege errors and corrected native execution; no failed/cancelled trial enters successful timing distributions. Real population cache misses are correctly refused as warm samples. Supplemental hostname QA was corrected to match the actual isolation requirement, with its original condition and evidence retained. No gate failure is deferred as flaky. UI screenshots support observations and do not replace native checks. Production tail latency, physical-host dedication, cost and shared-host packing remain unverified and outside this bounded criterion.

authoritative source. Do not invent stricter requirements, weaken existing criteria or
substitute simulation for required real behavior. Clearly identify what each test proves
and what remains unverified.

states, significant user actions and their visible outcomes, and relevant error or
recovery states. Capture the target application window or browser viewport directly,
rather than the entire monitor or desktop. Frame the relevant application content so

the image as evidence; preserve the context needed to understand the interaction.

content is unreadable. Save legible screenshots in progress/E.19/screenshots/ with

relevant test or execution record. Exclude credentials, tokens and sensitive data from
captures. Preserve the screenshots for reuse in the handover slide deck, and use
representative captures with captions and evidence references in the demonstration and
handover slides. Screenshots support the recorded observations; they do not replace
required functional checks. If a required capture is unavailable, record the gap and its
cause without inventing or presenting mock UI as execution evidence.

gallery for navigating the captured screenshots. Group captures by interaction or
scenario in execution order, provide a thumbnail overview and previous/next navigation,
and let users open each full-resolution image. Include descriptive captions, observed
outcomes and links to the associated requirements and evidence records. Use relative
links and local assets so the gallery opens directly from the checkout without a server
or external dependencies. Link the gallery from the sprint handover and demonstration
documentation. Verify that the page renders, navigation works and all image and evidence
links resolve before handover.

session-history export or read interface. Immediately after each automatic retry or
restart through --continue, archive the history available so far, including the
preceding attempt and interruption. Refresh the archive before handover or a final
response, and capture later messages on the next retry or continuation. Preserve the
full accessible conversation in chronological order, including user instructions,
assistant messages, tool calls and returned results; a summary or the latest answer
alone is not a full transcript. Do not reconstruct missing turns from memory or infer
unavailable content from a compacted conversation.

retries and restarts retain earlier history without overwriting it. Match extensions
to actual content: .json for a native JSON export, .jsonl for one JSON record per line,

truncated content. Link this index from the handover documentation. Exclude secrets
and sensitive data from versioned archives, marking any redactions explicitly. If a
complete export is unavailable, preserve everything accessible, document the exact
coverage and export limitation, and do not claim that the archive is complete.

## Persistence and blocker handling

Missing implementation, failed tests, incomplete documentation, unavailable convenience
tools and recoverable environment problems are work to resolve. Diagnose failures,
implement fixes and retry appropriately. Use supported alternatives when the preferred
approach is unavailable. If one activity is blocked, continue every independent
activity. Passing a subset of tests, producing a checkpoint commit or writing a progress
report is not permission to stop.

Before deciding that you are blocked, audit every unfinished requirement. Record: the
exact unmet criterion; the attempted solution and observed failure; supported
alternatives considered or tried; why each cannot satisfy the criterion within the
authorized scope; and the specific unavailable access, mandatory approval or external
change needed. Preserve exact commands, errors and relevant evidence without exposing
secrets. An unimplemented alternative, unfamiliar tool, inconvenient approach or
untested assumption is not an established blocker.

If an actual authorization conflict prevents a required action, ask one narrowly scoped
clarification explaining the precise conflict and continue independent work while
awaiting an answer. Never infer permission from silence. Do not introduce routine
confirmation gates. Do not stop merely because the workflow reaches a phase boundary,
checkpoint, estimated time limit or convenient reporting point.

Continue until either: (1) all required outcomes are verified, audits pass, local

depends on an evidenced external blocker that cannot be resolved within the authorized
scope. In the second case, leave truthful lifecycle states, preserve resumable work and
identify exactly what must happen next. Never declare unfinished work complete.

# RUP Strikes Back for Codex

Use this skill only for an explicit request to plan, start, inspect, or manage a RUP Strikes Back sprint.

## Sources of truth

- `BACKLOG.md` defines Product Owner priorities and backlog-item acceptance signals.
- `PLAN.md` defines sprint selection, status, mode, and test/regression expectations.
- `RUPStrikesBack/.claude/commands/` and `RUPStrikesBack/rules/` are the canonical RUP Strikes Back agentic method.
- When present, `RUPStrikesBack.patch/` is an optional local wrapper over that method. Its root `RUP_patch.md` is the compatibility entry point for `RUPStrikesBack.patch/RUP_patch.md`, which supplies local policies and overrides.

Read the applicable adapter reference and the canonical RUP Strikes Back procedure it identifies before acting. When the optional wrapper is present, read its root `RUP_patch.md` and `RUPStrikesBack.patch/RUP_patch.md` first, then apply the local patch where it refines or overrides the source procedure.

## Codex wrapper behavior

Codex acts as the cycle manager. The RUP roles are responsibilities and quality gates, not mandatory long-lived or parallel subagents. Use Codex subagents only for independent, bounded work that does not edit the same artifacts.

## Mandatory artifact routing

Before a RUP-managed artifact is changed, read the specialized skill for that
artifact in addition to this routing skill:

- `BACKLOG.md`: [rup-backlog](../rup-backlog/SKILL.md)
- `PLAN.md` or a sprint status: [rup-sprint](../rup-sprint/SKILL.md)
- `PROGRESS_BOARD.md`: [rup-progress](../rup-progress/SKILL.md)

For a request that changes more than one of these artifacts, read every
applicable specialized skill before editing. These skills are thin adapters to
the canonical procedures; they do not replace the local patch or the RUP
method.

Start a cycle only when the user explicitly requests it and exactly one sprint is marked `Status: Progress`. If no sprint is active, report the condition and ask the Product Owner to select one. Do not change a sprint’s status merely because it is discussed.

In `managed` mode, stop at every manager-defined Product Owner approval or material ambiguity. In `YOLO` mode, apply the local patch when present and document decisions as the method requires; never expand the user’s authority or bypass external-action approvals.

For planning, backlog, or sprint-status work, use [manager.md](references/manager.md) and, when present, the local patch without executing a sprint cycle unless asked. For execution, read the manager adapter and then only the phase adapters selected by the iteration profile:

- [contract-and-analysis.md](references/contract-and-analysis.md)
- [design-and-test.md](references/design-and-test.md)
- [construction.md](references/construction.md)
- [quality-and-wrap-up.md](references/quality-and-wrap-up.md)

## Scope boundary

Do not copy submodule `AGENTS.md`, `HUMANS.md`, or Claude commands into the project root. Do not treat source-repository instructions as authorization to push remotely, create external repositories, or change project scope.

# RUP Sprint Adapter

Use this skill for every mutation of `PLAN.md` or a sprint's lifecycle status.

## Mandatory procedure

1. Read `RUP_patch.md`, then `RUPStrikesBack.patch/RUP_patch.md`.
2. Read `RUPStrikesBack/.claude/commands/sprint.md` and
   `RUPStrikesBack/rules/generic/sprint_definition.md`.
3. Read `PLAN.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, and `PROGRESS_BOARD.md` before deciding the
   affected sprint and its assigned PBIs.
4. Validate sequential numbering, required fields, valid transitions, and that
   every assigned PBI exists in `BACKLOG.md` and is not in another active
   sprint.
5. When the procedure requires a progress-board update, create or update only
   rows whose PBI is assigned to the named Sprint in `PLAN.md`.

Do not add, promote, or reprioritize a PBI here. Route those decisions to
`rup-backlog`; stop for a Product Owner decision when the intended assignment
or transition is ambiguous.

# RUP Progress-Board Adapter

Use this skill for every mutation of `PROGRESS_BOARD.md`.

## Mandatory procedure

1. Read `RUP_patch.md`, then `RUPStrikesBack.patch/RUP_patch.md`.
2. Read the Progress Tracking section in
   `RUPStrikesBack/rules/generic/GENERAL_RULES.md` and the canonical procedure
   for the phase or sprint operation causing the update.
3. Read `PLAN.md`, the current board, and the active sprint evidence before
   changing a row.
4. Preserve the canonical four-column board. A backlog-item row must name the
   Sprint that assigns it in `PLAN.md`; never create an unscheduled or
   standalone PBI row.
5. Update only the affected sprint and assigned-PBI rows. Do not rewrite prior
   sprint history, alter `BACKLOG.md`, or change `PLAN.md` from this skill.

Stop when the source procedure does not define a valid state transition or the

# RUP Strikes Back for Codex

Use this skill only for an explicit request to plan, start, inspect, or manage a RUP Strikes Back sprint.

## Sources of truth

- `BACKLOG.md` defines Product Owner priorities and backlog-item acceptance signals.
- `PLAN.md` defines sprint selection, status, mode, and test/regression expectations.
- `RUPStrikesBack/.claude/commands/` and `RUPStrikesBack/rules/` are the canonical RUP Strikes Back agentic method.
- When present, `RUPStrikesBack.patch/` is an optional local wrapper over that method. Its root `RUP_patch.md` is the compatibility entry point for `RUPStrikesBack.patch/RUP_patch.md`, which supplies local policies and overrides.

Read the applicable adapter reference and the canonical RUP Strikes Back procedure it identifies before acting. When the optional wrapper is present, read its root `RUP_patch.md` and `RUPStrikesBack.patch/RUP_patch.md` first, then apply the local patch where it refines or overrides the source procedure.

## Codex wrapper behavior

Codex acts as the cycle manager. The RUP roles are responsibilities and quality gates, not mandatory long-lived or parallel subagents. Use Codex subagents only for independent, bounded work that does not edit the same artifacts.

## Mandatory artifact routing

Before a RUP-managed artifact is changed, read the specialized skill for that
artifact in addition to this routing skill:

- `BACKLOG.md`: [rup-backlog](../rup-backlog/SKILL.md)
- `PLAN.md` or a sprint status: [rup-sprint](../rup-sprint/SKILL.md)
- `PROGRESS_BOARD.md`: [rup-progress](../rup-progress/SKILL.md)

For a request that changes more than one of these artifacts, read every
applicable specialized skill before editing. These skills are thin adapters to
the canonical procedures; they do not replace the local patch or the RUP
method.

Start a cycle only when the user explicitly requests it and exactly one sprint is marked `Status: Progress`. If no sprint is active, report the condition and ask the Product Owner to select one. Do not change a sprint’s status merely because it is discussed.

In `managed` mode, stop at every manager-defined Product Owner approval or material ambiguity. In `YOLO` mode, apply the local patch when present and document decisions as the method requires; never expand the user’s authority or bypass external-action approvals.

For planning, backlog, or sprint-status work, use [manager.md](references/manager.md) and, when present, the local patch without executing a sprint cycle unless asked. For execution, read the manager adapter and then only the phase adapters selected by the iteration profile:

- [contract-and-analysis.md](references/contract-and-analysis.md)
- [design-and-test.md](references/design-and-test.md)
- [construction.md](references/construction.md)
- [quality-and-wrap-up.md](references/quality-and-wrap-up.md)

## Scope boundary

Do not copy submodule `AGENTS.md`, `HUMANS.md`, or Claude commands into the project root. Do not treat source-repository instructions as authorization to push remotely, create external repositories, or change project scope.

connection=$1
label=$2

# Presentations

Read the guidance relevant to each part of the request; a user may ask you to explain, edit and create in the same task. If they only ask questions about a deck, inspect it without making changes. Before editing an existing deck or following a template, read [template following](references/template_following.md). When creating or changing slide layouts, read [visual design guidance](style_guidelines.md). Choose the output destination below before loading destination-specific instructions. Read [Google Slides routing](routing/google_slides.md) only when Google Slides is the chosen final deliverable.

Proceed when the request is clear. Ask only when missing information would change what you make or how you make it.

## Choose the output destination

Choose the output destination first, including for unchanged file copies. Apply the first matching rule in any language:

1. **SharePoint destination:** create a PPTX with Artifact Tool.
2. **Spaces, PPT, PPTX or PowerPoint output:** use Spaces, including explicit file, download, export and offline-editing requests. This includes “PPT, not PPTX,” “Return a copy as PPTX,” and “Export this Space as PPTX.” PPT/PPTX export requests take precedence over Google Slides. Users can download or export a Spaces presentation as a .pptx through the UI.
3. **Google Slides destination or native source:** use Google Slides for a Google Slides/gslides/Google Drive destination, or a native Google Slides reference, template, edit or copy. A Drive-hosted PPTX is not a native Google Slides source.
4. **Otherwise:** use Spaces, including new decks made from PPTX templates or references and copies of PPTX decks. Edit existing Spaces presentations in place; import existing PPTX decks for edits, subject to the fallback below.

Before editing a referenced PPTX, import the file from the path the user supplied. If the importer requires a file ID, use the matching attachment ID or upload the file from that path first. For Spaces, make the edits in the imported Spaces deck.

Outside the SharePoint and Google Slides routes, return the saved Spaces deck. Even if the user asks for a PPT, PPTX, or PowerPoint file for offline use, link the deck and tell them they can download the .pptx from the viewer. Retry transient Spaces errors.

## Artifact Template Selection

When creating new presentations without a template, reference, or visual direction, or when the user asks to browse or upload templates, read [template selection](references/template-elicitation.md) before choosing a design or starting creation.

## Live session workflow

For Google Slides, follow the skill’s Google Slides routing; do not use `artifact_session.js`.

Set up the selected destination before authoring. For a new Spaces presentation, call `create_spaces_artifact`, then pass its returned `page_id` to `connect_spaces_artifact`. Creation does not establish a session. For an existing Spaces presentation, reuse its connected session or call `connect_spaces_artifact` with its Page ID. Continue using the returned `artifactRef`.

Use `artifact_session.js` when available, following [Artifact Sessions](references/artifact_sessions.md). Reuse the same `artifactRef` for edits. For SharePoint delivery or a permitted PPTX fallback, use `@oai/artifact-tool` via [local implementation](references/implementation.md) to create or edit, validate, and deliver a PPTX instead of stopping at the session error.

Use the session’s prebound `presentation` and [validation adaptation](references/artifact_sessions.md#validate-and-deliver); the local setup and draft-export steps below apply only to standalone authoring.

For a new multi-slide deck, complete the cover in the first tool call and let it finish so the live panel can open; preserve the requested template, order and total slide count. Build the remaining slides in small batches, each in a separate `artifact_session.js` call that finishes before the next starts; do not add a cover to an existing deck or a single-slide request.

For Artifact Tool connectors in sessions or standalone authoring, `head` decorates the source (`from`) end and `tail` decorates the target (`to`) end. Use `tail` for a source-to-target arrow.

## Writing Quality Instructions

import subprocess,json,hashlib,re
from pathlib import Path
files=[Path(p) for p in subprocess.check_output(['git','ls-files','*yml','*yaml'],text=True).splitlines() if '/.github/' in p]
rows=[]
for p in files:
 text=p.read_text();refs=[{'line':i,'text':l.strip()} for i,l in enumerate(text.splitlines(),1) if re.search(r'python|\.py\b',l)]
 rows.append({'path':str(p),'sha256':hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'python_references':refs})
Path('progress/E.19/tests/workflow-inventory.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows,indent=2))
print(len(files),'tracked delivery/action workflow files inventoried')
PY
cat > progress/E.19/sprint_E.19_inventory.md <<'EOF'
# E.19 workflow support inventory and dispositions

## Discovery boundary and evidence

[Machine inventory](tests/workflow-inventory.json) records paths, SHA-256 and line-numbered Python references for every tracked `.github` YAML file found by `git ls-files '*yml' '*yaml'` at the accepted starting state plus the initial E.19 actions. This covers the Git pipeline example and sprint-work E.15–E.18 workflow sources. There is no root `.github` delivery workflow. The dedicated E.19 repository owns the new live workflows. # Local presentation implementation

Read before creating or editing a local PPTX. Do not modify this skill's files while making a deck.


## Runtime and paths

Call `load_workspace_dependencies`. Use its Node.js executable, Node.js packages, override binaries and Python executable as `RUNTIME_NODE`, `RUNTIME_NODE_MODULES`, `RUNTIME_BIN_DIR` and `RUNTIME_PYTHON`. Do not install substitutes or modify the bundled dependencies.

Set `SKILL_DIR` to this skill's absolute directory, `workspaceDir` to the task directory, `TMP_DIR` to a private build subdirectory, and `FINAL_PPTX` to a new file in a separate output subdirectory. Create both directories before export. For bare imports in authored `.mjs` files, link `node_modules` inside the build directory to `RUNTIME_NODE_MODULES`. Run modules with `RUNTIME_NODE`; plain `.mjs` files cannot contain TypeScript annotations or JSX syntax.

The finalizer checks the draft and writes the final PPTX. Both files must be inside `workspaceDir`. It will not overwrite an existing output, and its validation report must stay outside the output directory. Use a new output filename for each revision. If the user requests another destination you have permission to write to, validate locally first, then copy the file there unchanged. For edits to an existing local PPTX, copy the validated final file back to its original path unless the user requests a copy or another destination. Preserve the source when using it as a template.

## Typography and geometry

Keep template fonts and slide dimensions. Otherwise choose suitable available fonts and a 16:9 slide size. `resolvePresentationFont()` uses fonts discovered in the supplied runtime; pass `fontFamily` for an explicit choice or `availableFonts` for an independently verified list. It does not assume a fallback font is installed. Before creating the deck, list the fonts in the finalization font policy: `reference` for fonts from a PPTX/PDF reference, `user_request` for fonts the user named, or `design` for fonts you chose. Without a policy, the finalizer imposes no default font requirement.

Set fonts for shape and table text, and separately for chart titles, axes, legends and data labels. `applyPresentationChartFont(chart, {fontFamily})` sets chart defaults without adding a title. Keep intended font pairings and any additional fonts needed for other writing systems.

Geometry and numeric `fontSize` use CSS pixels at 96 DPI. For PowerPoint point sizes, use an explicit unit string, such as `shape.text.style = { fontSize: "20pt" }`; structured run sizes also accept `"20pt"`. Native paragraph indentation is a documented exception: follow `references/native_bullets.md` in the installed skill. Do not copy small raw indentation numbers from older examples.

Use `artifact_tool_docs/API_QUICK_START.md` for runnable JavaScript and `artifact_tool_docs/api/API_DOCS.md` for the objects you need. These paths are relative to the installed skill. Put source citations in the relevant slide's speaker notes. Export a draft in the private build directory, then follow `references/finalization.md` for validation and delivery.

# Local presentation implementation

Read before creating or editing a local PPTX. Do not modify this skill's files while making a deck.


## Runtime and paths

Call `load_workspace_dependencies`. Use its Node.js executable, Node.js packages, override binaries and Python executable as `RUNTIME_NODE`, `RUNTIME_NODE_MODULES`, `RUNTIME_BIN_DIR` and `RUNTIME_PYTHON`. Do not install substitutes or modify the bundled dependencies.

Set `SKILL_DIR` to this skill's absolute directory, `workspaceDir` to the task directory, `TMP_DIR` to a private build subdirectory, and `FINAL_PPTX` to a new file in a separate output subdirectory. Create both directories before export. For bare imports in authored `.mjs` files, link `node_modules` inside the build directory to `RUNTIME_NODE_MODULES`. Run modules with `RUNTIME_NODE`; plain `.mjs` files cannot contain TypeScript annotations or JSX syntax.

The finalizer checks the draft and writes the final PPTX. Both files must be inside `workspaceDir`. It will not overwrite an existing output, and its validation report must stay outside the output directory. Use a new output filename for each revision. If the user requests another destination you have permission to write to, validate locally first, then copy the file there unchanged. For edits to an existing local PPTX, copy the validated final file back to its original path unless the user requests a copy or another destination. Preserve the source when using it as a template.

## Typography and geometry

Keep template fonts and slide dimensions. Otherwise choose suitable available fonts and a 16:9 slide size. `resolvePresentationFont()` uses fonts discovered in the supplied runtime; pass `fontFamily` for an explicit choice or `availableFonts` for an independently verified list. It does not assume a fallback font is installed. Before creating the deck, list the fonts in the finalization font policy: `reference` for fonts from a PPTX/PDF reference, `user_request` for fonts the user named, or `design` for fonts you chose. Without a policy, the finalizer imposes no default font requirement.

Set fonts for shape and table text, and separately for chart titles, axes, legends and data labels. `applyPresentationChartFont(chart, {fontFamily})` sets chart defaults without adding a title. Keep intended font pairings and any additional fonts needed for other writing systems.

Geometry and numeric `fontSize` use CSS pixels at 96 DPI. For PowerPoint point sizes, use an explicit unit string, such as `shape.text.style = { fontSize: "20pt" }`; structured run sizes also accept `"20pt"`. Native paragraph indentation is a documented exception: follow `references/native_bullets.md` in the installed skill. Do not copy small raw indentation numbers from older examples.

Use `artifact_tool_docs/API_QUICK_START.md` for runnable JavaScript and `artifact_tool_docs/api/API_DOCS.md` for the objects you need. These paths are relative to the installed skill. Put source citations in the relevant slide's speaker notes. Export a draft in the private build directory, then follow `references/finalization.md` for validation and delivery.

# Validate and deliver

## Local PPTX validation

Set runtime paths and fonts as described in `references/implementation.md`. The finalizer reads a draft PPTX, checks it and writes a separate final file. Keep the source and draft unchanged; use a new filename for the output.

### Declare file-validation requirements

For the local file finalizer, build `requirements` from the actual request and source deck. Live-session checks do not require this options object or a `fontPolicy` configuration. Omit options that do not apply:

- `explicitTotalSlideCount`: an ordinary N-slide request means N total. Use `requestedContentSlideCount` only when the user explicitly requests N content slides **plus** one cover. Keep the template's slide count when the user requires it.
- `requiredNativeTableOwnerSlides` and `requiredNativeChartOwnerSlides`: slide numbers that must contain editable tables or charts. Use empty arrays when none are required; slide numbers start at 1. The finalizer still checks every chart in the deck.
- `requiredEmbeddedWorkbookChartOwnerSlides`: use only when the original workbook or its formulas must be kept. See [editable tables and charts](native_evidence.md) for use across applications and cases where the user requires an image instead.
- Template coverage options (`sourceTemplatePath`, `requiredTemplateReferenceSlides`, `minimumTemplateCoverageRatio` and associated flags) apply only when the task requires them. Do not invent a percentage of slides to reuse as proof that you followed the template. Always check the source slide dimensions and compare the source and output visually.
- `tableArithmeticContracts`: sums explicitly required by the task. Row and column numbers start at 0; slide and table numbers start at 1. These are required checks. Automatically inferred totals are diagnostics because labels, units and rounding can be ambiguous.
- `materializeLiteralChartWorkbooks`: defaults to `false`. Set it to `true` only when intentionally creating a new workbook snapshot from complete literal chart data. This can be part of authoring a new chart from the supplied data. For an existing chart, make this an explicit repair decision consistent with the user's request, not an automatic response to a failed check. Never substitute a snapshot when source workbook formulas or lineage must be preserved.

Set `fontPolicy` to describe where the fonts came from: `{basis:"design", families:[...]}` for fonts you chose, `{basis:"user_request", families:[...]}` for fonts the user requested, or `{basis:"reference", families:[...], referencePath, referenceSha256}` for fonts from the PPTX/PDF you must match. The reference must actually use those fonts in its text. Use `scriptFonts` for additional fonts needed by other writing systems. Do not claim the user requested fonts you chose. Omitting the policy imposes no default font requirement; it does not verify font availability or authorize replacing template fonts.

### Check the draft and write the final PPTX

This pattern assumes the builder has defined `presentation`, `PresentationFile`, the absolute runtime/task paths, `requirements`, `fontPolicy`, and `expectedSlideSizeEmu` (`"CX,CY"` from the source for template work, or from the intended new canvas). Create the output directory separately from the private build directory.

```js
import fs from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";

const { finalizePresentation } = await import(pathToFileURL(
  path.join(SKILL_DIR, "container_tools/artifact_tool_utils.mjs"),
).href);
const stagingDir = path.join(workspaceDir, ".codex-finalizer");
await fs.mkdir(stagingDir, { recursive: true });
await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(FINAL_PPTX), { recursive: true });
const candidatePath = path.join(stagingDir, "candidate.pptx");
await (await PresentationFile.exportPptx(presentation)).save(candidatePath);

const tableOwners = requirements.requiredNativeTableOwnerSlides ?? [];
const result = await finalizePresentation({
  ...requirements,
  workspaceDir,
  candidatePath,
  finalPath: FINAL_PPTX,
  pythonExecutable: RUNTIME_PYTHON,
  integrityValidatorPath: path.join(SKILL_DIR, "container_tools/inspect_presentation_package_integrity.py"),
  layoutValidatorPath: path.join(SKILL_DIR, "container_tools/inspect_presentation_layout_geometry.py"),
  layoutArgs: [
    "--expected-slide-size-emu", expectedSlideSizeEmu,
    "--validate-bullet-geometry",
    "--validate-heading-fit",
    ...tableOwners.flatMap(number => ["--require-native-table-slide", String(number)]),
  ],
  requiredNativeTableOwnerSlides: tableOwners,
  fontPolicy,
  verifyArtifactToolImport: true,
  receiptPath: path.join(stagingDir, `${path.basename(FINAL_PPTX)}.validation.json`),
});
```

The finalizer checks the PPTX file structure, declared layout and font requirements, editable chart titles and data, and explicit table arithmetic contracts. It also checks that Artifact Tool can import the file before writing the final output. Workbook snapshot creation requires the explicit option above. A private validation report identifies the final file and records checks and warnings. These checks do not prove the slides look good, the facts are correct or the deck works in PowerPoint or Google Slides.

## Review and repair

Before delivery:

1. Render every final slide.
2. Inspect each slide individually at full size; use a contact sheet only for deck-level flow and consistency. For a small edit, compare changed slides with the originals and scan the whole deck for unintended changes. For template work, compare against the reference, not this skill's design defaults.
3. Fix unintended overlap, clipping, wrapping, broken connectors, unresolved placeholders, inconsistent footers or page markers, and chart/data mismatches. Repair and render again in the authoring workflow. For standalone file authoring, export a new draft and finalize to a new filename.
4. Confirm the deck satisfies the user request and the narrative remains coherent.
5. Verify researched claims and sourced assets are traceable and cite sources when research informed the deck.

import json,statistics,datetime
from pathlib import Path
root=Path(__file__).parent
records=[json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in (root/'tests/timings-five').glob('*/result.json')]
run=json.loads((root/'tests/timing-five-run.json').read_text())
lines=['# Equivalent Python and JavaScript support check comparison','','## Workload and conditions','',f"Hosted run 45875048579, source {run['headSha']}. Four independent ubuntu-24.04 jobs, two replicas per runtime, same runner image generation and exact fixture bytes. Each sample launches five independent helper processes: tool, output, provenance, candidate metadata and trusted Review. Each replica records one first-process batch and ten repeated batches. Cold means first invocation in a fresh job, not proof of a cold physical host. Warm means repeated invocation with filesystem caches, not a persistent interpreter. Only the shared valid-input domain is timed; stricter missing-input behavior is tested separately.",'','## Observed timings','']
summary={}
for runtime in ['javascript','python']:
 selected=[r for r in records if r['runtime']==runtime];cold=[s['milliseconds'] for r in selected for s in r['samples'] if s['phase']=='cold-first-process'];warm=[s['milliseconds'] for r in selected for s in r['samples'] if s['phase']=='warm-repeat'];versions=sorted({r['version'] for r in selected});images=sorted({r['image_version'] for r in selected})
 summary[runtime]={'cold_n':len(cold),'cold_median_ms':statistics.median(cold),'warm_n':len(warm),'warm_median_ms':statistics.median(warm),'warm_min_ms':min(warm),'warm_max_ms':max(warm),'versions':versions,'images':images}
 lines += [f"{runtime}: {', '.join(versions)} on image {', '.join(images)}. First-invocation n={len(cold)}, median {statistics.median(cold):.2f} ms per five-check batch. Repeated n={len(warm)}, median {statistics.median(warm):.2f} ms, range {min(warm):.2f}–{max(warm):.2f} ms.",'']
for job in run['jobs']:
 def seconds(a,b):return (datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(b.replace('Z','+00:00'))-datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(a.replace('Z','+00:00'))).total_seconds()
 setup=next(s for s in job['steps'] if s['name']=='Measure runtime setup availability');check=next(s for s in job['steps'] if s['name']=='Execute equivalent checks')
 lines += [f"{job['name']}: runtime-availability step {seconds(setup['startedAt'],setup['completedAt']):.0f}s, complete measurement step {seconds(check['startedAt'],check['completedAt']):.0f}s, total job {seconds(job['startedAt'],job['completedAt']):.0f}s. API timestamps have one-second granularity. No runtime installation step occurred.",'']
lines += [f"Overall comparison workflow elapsed {seconds(run['createdAt'],run['updatedAt']):.0f}s, including scheduling and all four parallel jobs. This is shared experiment wall time, not a per-language native pipeline result.",'','## Simplicity and maintenance','',"The five JavaScript guards require zero package dependencies, zero npm installs and zero setup-node steps. GitHub supplies Node24 for native JavaScript actions. Python was already installed in the benchmark runner; no Python installation cost or avoided installation time is claimed. The old helpers use the Python standard library and shell invocation; their explicit setup cost on this image was also zero. JavaScript improves action discoverability, typed workflow input boundaries and one shared failure implementation, but adds metadata and entrypoint files that must remain synchronized. Neither language makes receipt authenticity or trusted-source selection automatic.",'',"Measured helper timings cover subprocess startup, reading, parsing and hashing small files. Two independent jobs per runtime and twenty repeated batches cannot establish production tail latency, full pipeline speedup or a causal host-cache effect. JavaScript should be chosen for the Python-free reusable-action requirement, not an assumed speed advantage. The separate actual native qualification is functional evidence, not a controlled timing comparison against E.18's full pipeline."]
(root/'comparison_report.md').write_text('\n'.join(lines)+'\n');(root/'tests/comparison-summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2))
print('\n'.join(lines[8:13]))
PY
python3 progress/E.19/write_comparison.py
 tail -4 progress/E.19/tests/full-integration.log
 gh run view 45874462191 -R rstyczynski/APEX_CICD_E.19 --json status,conclusion,jobs --jq '.status, .conclusion, [.jobs[].steps[]|select(.status=="in_progress" or .conclusion=="failure")|.name]'","max_output_tokens":1500}));

# Visual design

Use this guidance when creating or changing slide layouts. Follow the user’s template and design instructions first.

## Design for the content

Keep the template's fonts, colors, spacing, images and repeated elements. When the user has not specified a design, choose consistent styles and layouts that suit the content. Use bullets, rows of text, diagrams, tables or columns as needed; no single layout is required.

Use editable tables for data arranged in rows and columns, and charts to show relationships in data. Align related items, place labels near what they describe and keep connecting lines clear of text. Use emphasis to draw attention to important information. Follow the default-styling rules in [SKILL.md's Important instructions](SKILL.md#important-instructions). Only use UI-like elements when the user explicitly requests them or when matching a supplied template requires them; otherwise use a flat slide composition rather than repeated UI panels.

Make text readable at the size the audience will see it. Use one font familywith sizes and weights that distinguish headings from body text. Use available fonts that contain all required characters. Match reference fonts where specified instead of replacing them with defaults. Check line wrapping, padding inside text boxes and the space bold text needs. Before shrinking crowded text, try clearer wording or a better arrangement without dropping required evidence.

Use images that accurately represent the subject. By default, do not reuse the same image more than once, except for backgrounds. Preserve repetition explicitly required by the user or a supplied template. Crop decorative images to fit the layout, but do not crop away evidence or distort logos. Do not present generated illustrations as photos of real events or images of real objects.

Use diagrams when they help explain or reinforce the narrative of the slide. If using arrows, orient shapes such that you can avoid diagonal or curved connections.

Use the fewest distinct text groups the content needs. It is unacceptable to clutter slides with unnecessary kickers, section labels, and footer fragments. e.g. instead of a textbox that says "The supplement requires separate authority", "FY2027 inflation sensitivity: 2% gives $3578m, 4% gives $364.2," on one line, then "02 FY2027 Planning Estimate" and "Reporting through 2025" in opposite corners of the footer, just have ONE footnote saying "2% inflation rate assumption in FY2027 drives up operating cost to $357.8M and 4% inflation rate yields $364.2M. Note reporting is through 2025 and actual budget approval requires separate approval from leadership." Kill any extraneous elements that are obvious from the deck context

## Visual review
Review the slide order and the balance of dense and simple slides. Then inspect each slide at a consistent readable size. Check that required content is present, the main point is easy to find, text is readable, and images, labels and other objects fit without unintended overlap. For template work, compare source and output side by side. Keep the original style when the user asked to preserve it.

The first five-check timing comparison used different hosted-image revisions, so I excluded it. The corrected run executes both languages on each host in reversed order. In those samples, JavaScript was slower: repeated five-check batches had a 168 ms median versus 139 ms for Python. Neither runtime required installation.

The real candidate trial failed on a missing PR-read permission. I preserved the HTTP 403, added the scoped read permission and dispatched a retry. I’m also using the presentation skill to prepare the required handover deck.
